distractorExplanations.d: Titles are incomplete evidence; skipping the second passage cannot show what both texts support.

prompt: An advisor tells a candidate to study Danielson domains and lesson-plan steps for “the Praxis” required for program entry. The listed tests are Core 5713, 5723, and 5733. What should the candidate actually prepare?

options.text: Danielson domains and lesson-plan steps, because Core Academic Skills is the pedagogy exam for those listed codes
Classroom-management scenarios, which appear as a fourth subtest on combined 5752
Principles of Learning and Teaching only, which replaces Core Writing for most states
Reading, writing, and math academic skills; pedagogy belongs to PLT or subject assessments, not 5713–5733

explanation: Praxis Core Academic Skills for Educators measures college-ready reading, writing, and mathematics used for entry into many teacher-prep programs. Classroom management, lesson design, and Danielson-style observation rubrics belong to PLT or content assessments, not 5713/5723/5733. Studying the wrong Praxis title wastes the Core clock.

distractorExplanations.a: 5713–5733 are academic-skills tests; Danielson domains are not Core content.
distractorExplanations.b: 5752 is still Reading, Writing, and Math; it does not add a classroom-management subtest.
distractorExplanations.c: PLT does not substitute for Core Writing 5723 when a program lists Core as the entry gate.
